text:
maria: FYI support ticket escalated — several customers reporting missing audit events for a ~3hr window overnight. noticed this for tenants: acct-7, acct-19, acct-42. forwarding logs now.
support_sam: thanks, I saw the alert too. initial check: s3 manifests exist but some object keys are zero-byte. looks related to forwarder v2.1.3.
raj: @maria can you paste the S3 prefixes and one example manifest id? want to grep checksums.
maria: s3://redwood-audit/tenants/acct-7/2026-03-13/manifest-000132.json - pasted in support ticket. example batch key inside manifest: events/2026/03/13/02/14/evt-7a9f.gz (size 0)
jordan: copying small repro steps: 1) list objects for that prefix 2) head-object on gz 3) run `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-audit --key "events/2026/03/13/02/14/evt-7a9f.gz"` returns `ContentLength: 0`
sec-bot: automated alert: forwarder-decrypt-errors increased by 1200 between 02:00-05:00 UTC; top error: "KMS.DecryptAccessDeniedException" for alias/rdw-forwarder-accessor
sophie: aha — we rotated the accessor alias this morning as part of scheduled KMS rollover. did we update forwarder IAM/KMS grants for the new alias?
raj: checking KMS key policy: the new alias points to key ARN arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-rotated, but the forwarder principal `iam::987654:role/audit-forwarder` is only listed on the old key policy. that would cause decrypt failures and the forwarder to emit zero-byte placeholders.
maria: that matches timeline. customers started seeing gaps right after rotation at ~02:05 UTC. support wants a replay plan and root-cause blurb for compliance teams.
jordan: repro checklist we used: 
```
# list suspect manifests\aws s3 ls s3://redwood-audit/tenants/acct-7/2026-03-13/ --recursive
# check head-object for each event key
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-audit --key "events/2026/03/13/02/14/evt-7a9f.gz"
# check CloudTrail for KMS decrypt denies
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-13T02:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-13T05:00:00Z
```
raj: verified CloudTrail entries show `DecryptAccessDenied` for the forwarder role on the rotated key; timestamps line up.
support_sam: what's the safest mitigation to get events into SIEM asap? customers want completeness in next 24h.
sophie: mitigation plan: 1) update rotated key policy to include `arn:aws:iam::987654:role/audit-forwarder` with Decrypt permissions (short-term rollback). 2) restart forwarder workers so they retry previously failed batches. 3) run targeted backfill for zero-byte objects.
maria: can we avoid granting permanent access to rotated key? compliance prefers granting the forwarder role access on a usage-limited grant and rotate alias mapping.
raj: agreed — do a one-time KMS grant with condition `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent`? Not possible for service roles. Instead propose creating a short-lived grant via KMS Grant API and then have backfill use current key to re-encrypt? But forwarder needs to decrypt existing ciphertext to re-encrypt to new alias.
jordan: practical playbook I've used before: 
1) add forwarder role to rotated key policy temporarily (audit log entry + slack approval)
2) run forwarder backfill mode: `forwarder backfill --tenant acct-7 --start 2026-03-13T02:00Z --end 2026-03-13T05:00Z --retry-zero-byte` 
3) verify objects are non-zero and checksums match manifest SHA256 sums (script below)
4) revoke the temporary key policy entry after successful replay.

checksum script snippet:
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit/tenants/acct-7/2026-03-13/events/evt-7a9f.gz - | sha256sum
# compare to manifest sha256 field
```

sophie: one more thing — the SIEM connector expects `actor_id` field but some recent manifests contain `actor_identity` (we had a schema aliasing change in rdr-ingest v4). When we replay, forwarder will preserve original keys, so SIEM mapping may drop those events. we should add a temporary shim in the forwarder mapping layer to map `actor_identity -> actor_id` for replays.
maria: good catch. support needs a note for customers: why data missing and what we'll do. draft blurb: "Root cause: KMS accessor rotation created a key policy mismatch — audit forwarder could not decrypt several batches and wrote zero-byte placeholders. Impact: incomplete audit export for a 3hr window for a subset of tenants. Remediation: temporary key policy grant, replay of failed batches, checksum validation, and schema-mapping shim to ensure SIEM compatibility. We will revoke temporary grants once replay completes and provide a verification report."
support_sam: please include expected ETA: policy change + forwarder restart = ~15-30m; replay duration depends on volume (estimate 2-6h for listed tenants). I'll inform customers with that window.
raj: steps I'm running now: 1) open internal PR to modify rotated key policy (link pasted) 2) create monitoring alert for `forwarder_replay_success` and `manifest_zero_byte_reduction`
sec-bot: action recorded: KMS policy change requested by raj at 2415004820.
jordan: after policy update I'll trigger `forwarder backfill` and post progress updates every 30m. will attach sample validation command output to thread.
sophie: I pushed a temporary mapping rule to staging forwarder: `map actor_identity -> actor_id` behind flag `replay-schema-shim=true`. once replay runs, enable flag in prod for backfill job only.
maria: thanks team. after replay, we should produce a compliance report with: list of tenants affected, manifests reprocessed, checksums before/after, SIEM ingest confirmation, and the KMS policy audit entry.
support_sam: noted — I'll collect customer consent where required and update ticket.
raj: once we revoke grant I'll attach the CloudTrail audit entry to the report. closing loop in ~8h or earlier with updates. :thumbsup:
